meta.description: Sunday digest of Colorado affordable housing news. One edition per week, Monday to Sunday, written from official releases and checked newsrooms. Each edition is a Markdown file in this folder.
meta.schedule: Sundays, about 6:40 am Mountain Time; published on the site when the weekly pull request merges

editions.title: Colorado Housing Week: Nov 16 – 22, 2026
summary: CHFA's 2026 Round Two tax credits went to 9 of 26 applications, for 845 rental homes; 8 of the 9 are in metro Denver, and no rural project won.
The governor asked for a second federal flood declaration, this time with household aid in four counties; 271 primary homes were destroyed or unlivable from the second storm.
A federal judge blocked HUD's rewrite of the homelessness grant program, protecting supportive housing renewals for now.
HUD's final mixed-status rule takes effect Dec 14, and two lawsuits were filed against it.
The 30-year rate rose to 7.28%, ending a four-week slide.

editions.title: Colorado Housing Week: Nov 9 – 15, 2026
summary: DOLA's first statewide housing needs assessment: one in three households is cost-burdened, and the state needs about 30,600 new homes a year through 2036.
The flood damage count now includes households, through FEMA's Individual Assistance program; 311 displaced households have had emergency lodging.
A final Forest Service rule lets administrative site leases back a loan, taking effect around Dec 2.
The Senate advanced a permitting bill that reaches HOME and CDBG projects, 73–25; Hickenlooper voted yes and Bennet no.
The 30-year rate fell to 7.11%, and Colorado home sales fell nearly 19% from last October.

editions.title: Colorado Housing Week: Nov 2 – 8, 2026
summary: The southwest Colorado floods hit twice, and about 700 homes are damaged; the federal request still covers public infrastructure only.
Prop NN passed and Amendment 87 leads, which makes state housing money a little safer.
HUD opened an Express Lane for FHA construction loans on new LIHTC deals.
Polis's final budget request leaves a $1.6 billion gap; he presents it Nov 12.
The 30-year mortgage rate eased to 7.18%; 65% of metro Denver's October sales involved seller concessions.
